A3_lohto_head_to_head.protocol: leave-out-highest-temperature per series; all predictors see the identical information set (that series' lower-T points plus every other series' lower-T points)

A6_replicate_irreducible_noise_floor.note: replicate dispersion is measured on the SAME (material, environment, concentration, temperature) cell across independent literature entries; it involves no model and bounds what any predictor can achieve on this dataset

filters.replicate_rule: median of rates at identical (series, temperature)

dataset.rights_note: NIST public data (NIST CORR-DATA); no external download performed

known_limitations: NIST CORR-DATA aggregates heterogeneous literature sources; replicate spread at fixed (series, T) can exceed the temperature effect
concentration_text is free text; the numeric parse used for P3b takes the first number and ignores units/qualifiers
series are chemical-process environments, mostly not marine atmospheric; the marine/chloride stratum is small and power-flagged
no pressure/phase metadata: the [0,150] degC window is a proxy for the aqueous liquid regime, not a verified phase constraint
target_interpretation.role: environmental/thermal severity input to a barrier-corrosion score; grants no coating-barrier, batch-release, optimizer or product-performance authority
target_interpretation.target: log10 corrosion rate of BARE metal/alloy substrate, mm/yr

verdict.A1_detail: median per-series R^2 = 0.452 with only 12.0% of series at R^2 >= 0.90; the sign is right (76.0% have Ea > 0) but the magnitude of scatter means a 2-parameter Arrhenius fit is not an adequate law here.
verdict.A2_vantHoff_scale: CORROBORATED_IN_SCALE_NOT_IN_VALUE: 68.4% of positive-Ea series fall inside the [0.5x, 2x] van 't Hoff Q10=2 band, and the median implied Q10 over 25-35 degC is 1.76 -- the textbook 'doubles per 10 degC' rule OVERSTATES the median observed temperature sensitivity.
verdict.A3_head_to_head: NO_PREDICTOR_SIGNIFICANTLY_BETTER: best MAE 0.614 log10 (factor 4.1) vs carry-forward null 0.662; every paired sign test has p >= 0.30. The 2-parameter Arrhenius fit ties the 300-tree HistGBM QSPR. The zero-parameter van 't Hoff Q10=2 rule is the WORST predictor, consistent with A2.
verdict.A5_red_team: Shuffling rate values across temperatures within each series drops median R^2 from 0.452 to 0.289 -- a real but MODEST collapse, showing that a large part of the apparent Arrhenius linearity is small-sample (4-6 point) fitting artefact, not physics.
verdict.A6_ceiling: The measured model-free replicate dispersion on identical (material, environment, concentration, temperature) cells is 0.705 log10 mean pairwise |diff| (451 pairs). The best predictor's LOHTO MAE is 0.614 log10. Prediction error is therefore of the SAME ORDER as the dataset's own source-to-source disagreement: the temperature-extrapolation ceiling on NIST CORR-DATA is set by data heterogeneity, not by model class.
verdict.consequence_for_the_module: This bounds the corrosion-rate severity input: the wide calibrated intervals reported by corr-rate-conformal-v1 are HONEST, not a modelling failure -- a factor ~4-5 spread is the irreducible floor of this data source. Adding a physical temperature law does NOT tighten them. Any real improvement requires protocol-controlled primary corrosion-rate series, not a better estimator.
verdict.headline: The Arrhenius law is REFUTED as an adequate per-series description of NIST CORR-DATA corrosion rates, while the van 't Hoff Q10 rule is CORROBORATED IN SCALE but not in value; and on a strict leave-out-highest-temperature test NO predictor -- physical or ML -- is statistically distinguishable from a carry-forward null.
